profile.summary: PaulBRamos is a Mid-Level JavaScript developer with specialized expertise in jQuery's core DOM manipulation and internal systems. His contributions focus on fixing subtle bugs in jQuery's utility methods (e.g., `.width()`, `insertAfter`) and maintaining the project's unit test suite. The developer demonstrates strong debugging skills for browser rendering quirks, particularly around CSS layout and DOM insertion edge cases. While his experience is deeply rooted in jQuery's legacy codebase, his work shows proficiency in DOM traversal, test maintenance, and collaborative code review processes. There is no evidence of modern JavaScript frameworks or backend systems in his contributions.
skill_evidence: Fixed `.width()` returning percentage when parent has `display: none` (PR #9945), demonstrating deep CSS layout and computed style debugging
Resolved `insertAfter`/`insertBefore` edge case where source and destination elements are identical (PR #4087), showing DOM traversal mastery
Maintained `manipulation.js` unit tests with styling fixes (PR #12756), proving familiarity with jQuery's QUnit test suite
Coordinated with `@erickrdch` to avoid duplicate work on `manipulation.js` (PR #12756), illustrating collaborative development practices
Addressed fragment cache removal in jQuery internals (PR #11989), indicating knowledge of jQuery's internal optimization patterns
Debugged browser-specific rendering inconsistencies in DOM measurement methods (PR #9945), showcasing cross-browser compatibility skills
Fixed test flakiness caused by styling issues in unit tests (PR #12756), demonstrating test maintenance expertise
Reproduced and fixed subtle DOM insertion bugs requiring manual DOM inspection (PR #4087), proving edge-case debugging capabilities
